Chapter 12 — Foreign Trade of Pakistan (Foreign Trade of Pakistan)

Importance of foreign trade

In our economy foreign trade has great importance, as becomes known from the following things:

1. Important part of domestic production

The value of the exports and imports of Pakistan is an important part of the gross domestic product (G.D.P) of Pakistan, because goods equal to approximately the eleventh part of GDP are exported.

2. Dependence of industrial development

The industrial development of Pakistan depends on this, that by exporting as many goods as possible sufficient foreign exchange be earned, and with it machines, raw material, spare parts, chemical goods, mineral oil, petrol, fuel and other development equipment be imported, so that national industry can develop.

3. External loans

Pakistan has taken much loan from abroad to complete economic schemes and development projects; for its return and the payment of interest it is necessary that, by increasing exports, foreign exchange be earned. This loan has been taken from the Consortium (Consortium) (i.e. partner countries). In it these countries and institutions are included: Japan, America, Germany, France, Canada, Italy, World Bank and International Development Agency etc. Besides them Pakistan has also taken loans from Islamic countries, in which these are included: Abu Dhabi, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the Islamic Development Bank etc.

4. Problem of return of loan and interest

The imports of Pakistan are more than its exports; therefore a continuous deficit has been running in the balance of payments. Further, for development purposes it has taken much loan from foreign countries, because of which an increase has kept occurring in the annual amount of interest. Therefore there is need that exports be increased as much as possible, so that the burden of loan and interest on the country can be reduced.

Major exports of Pakistan (Major Exports of Pakistan)

Here we take a separate review of the exports of Pakistan:

1. Cotton thread (Cotton Yarn)

Among the exports of Pakistan the thing earning very much foreign exchange is cotton thread (cotton yarn). In 1970-71 yarn worth only 34 crore rupees was exported, whereas in the first nine months of 2009-10, 121 crore dollars’ worth.

Chapter 12 — Foreign Trade of Pakistan (Foreign Trade of Pakistan)

Importance of foreign trade

In our economy foreign trade has great importance, as becomes known from the following things:

1. Important part of domestic production

The value of the exports and imports of Pakistan is an important part of the gross domestic product (G.D.P) of Pakistan, because goods equal to approximately the eleventh part of GDP are exported.

2. Dependence of industrial development

The industrial development of Pakistan depends on this, that by exporting as many goods as possible sufficient foreign exchange be earned, and with it machines, raw material, spare parts, chemical goods, mineral oil, petrol, fuel and other development equipment be imported, so that national industry can develop.

3. External loans

Pakistan has taken much loan from abroad to complete economic schemes and development projects; for its return and the payment of interest it is necessary that, by increasing exports, foreign exchange be earned. This loan has been taken from the Consortium (Consortium) (i.e. partner countries). In it these countries and institutions are included: Japan, America, Germany, France, Canada, Italy, World Bank and International Development Agency etc. Besides them Pakistan has also taken loans from Islamic countries, in which these are included: Abu Dhabi, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the Islamic Development Bank etc.

4. Problem of return of loan and interest

The imports of Pakistan are more than its exports; therefore a continuous deficit has been running in the balance of payments. Further, for development purposes it has taken much loan from foreign countries, because of which an increase has kept occurring in the annual amount of interest. Therefore there is need that exports be increased as much as possible, so that the burden of loan and interest on the country can be reduced.

Major exports of Pakistan (Major Exports of Pakistan)

Here we take a separate review of the exports of Pakistan:

1. Cotton thread (Cotton Yarn)

Among the exports of Pakistan the thing earning very much foreign exchange is cotton thread (cotton yarn). In 1970-71 yarn worth only 34 crore rupees was exported, whereas in the first nine months of 2009-10, 121 crore dollars’ worth.
